ranked_hypotheses.summary: Proximate cause, well supported: shipping-svc calls to parcelhub-api /v2/rates exceeded the 600/min quota. parcelhub returned 429s with Remaining: 0, which shipping-svc surfaced as 502s and customers saw as 'shipping unavailable'. Every ERROR line is this 429 type, and parcelhub calls sit at exactly 600/min at both error peaks (12:10Z and 12:45Z). The arithmetic fits: 1 - 600/1010 is about 41%, matching the observed 41%. As a root cause, this hypothesis says the volume driver is organic demand, which the parcelhub plan cannot absorb, as in the past holiday-peak incident. The marketing-svc Black Week campaign is now a weak link. It deployed at 11:20Z, yet quote volume was still a normal 365/min at 11:50Z, so a later go-live would be needed. Points for organic load: after the rollback, volume at 12:30Z was still elevated at 580/min versus 365, and errors recurred at 12:45Z with no redeploy, which a demand-driven cause explains better than v5.2.0. Remediation if true: raise the plan tier or cache quotes per basket. Next check: pull per-minute quote_requests_per_min and parcelhub calls (accepted and rejected) for 11:50Z-13:00Z, and get the campaign's actual go-live timestamp.

The v5.2.0 carrier-selection release (11:55Z) drove the excess load that exhausted the parcelhub quota. It did not cause parse errors; all ERROR lines are 429s. Two mechanisms are possible. (a) v5.2.0 makes extra parcelhub calls per quote. The earlier 'no fan-out' rebuttal is withdrawn because parcelhub_requests_per_min is pinned at the quota at 12:10Z and may count only accepted calls. (b) PHX-skipped quotes come back incomplete, so clients re-request them, inflating inbound quote volume. Timing supports this: the 365 to 1010 surge falls between 11:50Z and 12:10Z, bracketing the 11:55Z deploy. The dip to 580 quotes/min and 7.5% errors at 12:30Z comes three minutes after the 12:27Z rollback. Against it: errors recurred at 12:45Z, with parcelhub back at 600/min and no redeploy. Post-rollback volume (580) also stayed well above the 365 baseline. Both points imply another load source unless v5.2.0 instances lingered. Remediation if true: keep v5.2.0 rolled back and fix the call or re-request behaviour. Next check: per-minute quote volume around 11:55Z and 12:27Z, parcelhub calls per quote in v5.2.0 traces, and the instance version on the 12:41Z and 12:47Z error lines.

Client or checkout-web retries of failed quotes amplify load. After the first 429s, re-requests inflate quote volume (1010/min) and keep parcelhub pinned at 600/min. When errors briefly fall, retries fall too (580/min at 12:30Z), and then the cycle repeats (12:45Z). This needs an initial trigger, since errors were 0.3% at 11:50Z, so it amplifies h1 or h2 rather than replacing them. It cannot be told apart from organic traffic without unique-basket or session counts. checkout-web retry and volume metrics returned nothing. Remediation if true: fix the client retry policy (backoff, honour Retry-After). Next check: unique baskets or sessions versus quote requests per minute, and the checkout-web retry config.

The log.level change from info to debug at 12:05Z added overhead and caused or prolonged failures. This is weak. The first 429 (12:01:14Z) predates the change. All errors are upstream 429s, not timeouts or resource errors. The error rate tracks parcelhub call volume, not anything debug logging would explain.

facts.statement: shipping-svc error rate was 0.3% at 11:50Z and rose to 41.0% at 12:10Z.
The first ERROR log in the window is at 12:01:14Z: POST /quotes returned 502 because parcelhub-api POST /v2/rates returned 429 Too Many Requests with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0.
Error rate fell to 7.5% at 12:30Z, while parcelhub_requests_per_min was 540 and quote_requests_per_min was 580.
Error rate rose again to 38.0% at 12:45Z, with parcelhub_requests_per_min at 600.
At 12:10Z, parcelhub_requests_per_min was 600 (the rate-limit ceiling in the 429 log messages) while quote_requests_per_min was 1010. The error rate was 41.0% at that point.

All five ERROR log lines in 11:30Z–13:00Z are the same type: 502 caused by a 429 from parcelhub-api /v2/rates. They are at 12:01:14, 12:04:52, 12:15:40, 12:41:22 and 12:47:35Z. No timeout or connection-error ERROR lines appear in the window.
A WARN at 12:02:30Z reports 'v5.2.0 carrier-selection: unknown carrier code PHX in rate response, skipping'. It is a separate warning and does not match the ERROR lines.

The shipping-svc error signal is dominated by parcelhub-api 429 responses, with no timeout or connection errors visible in the ERROR logs. Customer-facing 'shipping unavailable' is consistent with these 502s.

assumptions.statement: One targeted per-minute pull of quote volume, parcelhub accepted/rejected calls, and unique baskets for 11:50Z-13:00Z would separate the v5.2.0, organic/campaign, and retry drivers.
assumptions.basis: Each driver predicts a different shape: a step at 11:55Z and a drop at 12:27Z for v5.2.0, a gradual rise tied to sessions for organic or campaign traffic, and repeat requests per basket for retries.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Run the pull and compare the volume curve against the 11:55Z deploy and the 12:27Z rollback, and compare quotes per unique basket.

recommended_actions.action: Pull per-minute quote_requests_per_min and parcelhub /v2/rates call counts (accepted and rejected) for 11:50Z-13:00Z, and confirm the Black Week campaign's actual go-live timestamp in marketing-svc.
recommended_actions.rationale: h1 is the leading explanation but depends on whether organic demand, not the v5.2.0 deploy, drove the volume. The post-rollback volume of 580/min and the 12:45Z recurrence need to be explained by demand data, and the campaign timing needs confirming.

recommended_actions.action: Mitigate the parcelhub quota exhaustion while the root cause is confirmed: request a temporary quota or plan-tier increase from parcelhub, and/or enable per-basket quote caching in shipping-svc to reduce outbound /v2/rates calls.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 429s with Remaining: 0 directly cause the 502s and 'shipping unavailable' errors. Reducing outbound calls or raising the limit addresses the proximate failure regardless of which upstream driver is confirmed.

recommended_actions.action: Keep v5.2.0 rolled back and verify that no v5.2.0 instances are still serving traffic, by checking the instance version on the 12:41Z and 12:47Z error lines.
recommended_actions.rationale: Errors recurred at 12:45Z with no redeploy, and post-rollback volume stayed above baseline. Confirming that v5.2.0 instances are fully gone tests whether the release is still a contributor before any fix is re-deployed.

recommended_actions.action: Measure parcelhub calls per quote in v5.2.0 traces and compare per-minute quote volume around the 11:55Z deploy and the 12:27Z rollback, to test whether the carrier-selection release adds fan-out or incomplete-quote re-requests.
recommended_actions.rationale: The surge timing brackets the deploy, but the post-rollback volume does not fully fit. Per-quote call counts would show whether v5.2.0 multiplies parcelhub load, which decides whether the release needs a fix before re-deploy.

recommended_actions.action: Compare unique baskets or sessions against quote requests per minute, and review the checkout-web retry configuration (backoff, Retry-After handling).
recommended_actions.rationale: Separating retry-driven volume from organic traffic is the only way to confirm the amplification loop. If retries are confirmed, fixing the client retry policy reduces load on the quota without changing upstream capacity.

recommended_actions.action: Revert the shipping-svc log.level from debug back to info as low-risk hygiene, and do not treat it as a root-cause fix.
recommended_actions.rationale: Debug logging adds some overhead and should not persist in production. The evidence is weak that it caused the failures, since the first 429 predates the change, so this is housekeeping only.

evidence_support.rationale: The core facts match their cited rows: the 429s with Remaining: 0 (log:inc10:0003/0005/0006/0008/0010), 600 rpm at the peaks (metric:inc10:rpm:0002/0004), 1010 vs 365 quotes, and the rollback timing. Some statements are weakly cited, such as data-absence claims backed only by existing samples. One assumption has the timeline wrong: it says the 12:02:30Z WARN (log:inc10:0004) comes 'shortly before' the 12:01:14Z 429.

fact_assumption_separation.rationale: Facts are observational and properly cited, but heavily duplicated. The assumptions list holds stale, contradictory leftovers: it claims no deploy or error-rate data was retrieved, and one entry calls v5.2.0 'the likely trigger' via past:inc10:0001, both at odds with the stated facts and the ranking. Most assumptions do give a basis and a way to verify.

recommended_actions.rationale: Mitigates the proximate parcelhub quota exhaustion with a plan-tier increase or per-basket caching, matching past:inc10:0002 and the answer key. Requests targeted per-minute data and the campaign go-live time, and adds sensible low-risk checks: lingering v5.2.0 instances, client retry policy, and reverting debug logging.

fell_for_trap.rationale: The top hypothesis h1 places the cause on the parcelhub-api limit and explicitly notes that errors recurred at 12:45Z after the rollback (metric:inc10:err:0004). It ties the 12:30Z dip to falling volume (metric:inc10:quotes:0003), not to the rollback, and keeps v5.2.0 (deploy:inc10:0002, log:inc10:0004) as a lower-ranked contributor.
